short: Listener-tested sentence synthesis from ECoG, alongside concurrent work; its articulatory-intermediate gain is not isolated from extra supervision, and intelligibility rests on closed word pools.
position: All three changed components are standard: sentence waveforms (M08) extend formant synthesis [[2]](#ref-2) and spectrogram decoding [[3]](#ref-3); mimed transfer (M04) repeats [[3]](#ref-3); the articulatory pipeline (M06) first implements a proposed architecture [[4]](#ref-4), with its benefit shown in one participant. Its lasting contribution is listener-tested sentence synthesis from ECoG, alongside concurrent work [[5]](#ref-5). The attribution to articulation is not isolated: the intermediate is trained from phonological features, the participant's MFCCs and 18 place-manner targets set from phoneme labels (Methods), so the 0.54 dB MCD gain over the direct decoder (Fig. 2e) mixes articulatory structure with extra supervision; later linear decoders on other recordings favoured direct decoding [[6]](#ref-6). Intelligibility is measured only with closed word pools, without a reported chance WER. Whether articulatory structure, not added supervision, helps neural speech decoding remains untested.

unverified_from_evaluation: Littlejohn et al., Nature Neuroscience 2025 (doi:10.1038/s41593-025-01905-6), streaming ECoG voice synthesis, proposed for the M08 state of the art: not in the wiki, so its metric and value could not be checked against a source; not added to the review.
Mimed MCD value: the target reports it only graphically (Fig. 3d of the author manuscript); no numeric value was read from the figure.
verification_status.notes: Figure numbers follow the PMC author manuscript (PMC9714519) read in the wiki: Fig. 2e = training-data comparison of articulatory vs direct decoder, Fig. 3 = mimed speech, Fig. 4 = kinematic state-space.
